question.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}-2x+50=0$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
question.worked_solution:
We first move the constant to the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x+50 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2x & =-50\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x & =-50 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot x+{1}^{2}-{1}^{2} & =-50 \\ (x-1)^{2}-1 & =-50 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =-49\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=-1,\,q=-49,$ and $p+q=-50.$

We now solve the equation using the square root method.

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =-49 \\ x-1 & =\pm \sqrt{-49} \\ x-1 & =\pm 7\,\text{i} \\ x & =1\pm 7\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=1+7\,\text{i}$ and $x=1-7\,\text{i}.$
